record.context_brief: basic existence of nondegenerate k-orbit polytopes
record.original_question: For every pair of integers k ≥ 1 and n ≥ 3, does there exist a k-orbit n-polytope such that no rank-2 section is a digon?

evidence.quote: Problem 10. Are there k-orbit n-polytopes for every k ≥ 1 and every n ≥ 3 such that no section of rank 2 is a digon?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
An abstract n-polytope is a partially ordered set (with minimum and maximum elements) whose elements are called faces, ranked by rank in {-1, 0, 1, ..., n}, satisfying the usual diamond condition and strong flag-connectedness; flags are maximal chains of faces. The automorphism group acts on flags, and the polytope is called a k-orbit polytope if this action has exactly k orbits. A section of rank 2 is the interval [F, G] between a face F of rank i-1 and a face G of rank i+1 with F < G; such a section is a "digon" if it contains exactly two faces of rank i (so the section is combinatorially a polygon with two edges).

Question: Is it true that for every pair of integers k ≥ 1 and n ≥ 3, there exists a k-orbit abstract n-polytope none of whose rank-2 sections is a digon?
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is listed as one of 35 open problems on k-orbit abstract polytopes. Related existence questions about k-orbit polytopes (e.g., realization of 2-orbit classes as polytopes) remain active research; no search result indicates a complete resolution of the nondegeneracy existence question for all k ≥ 1 and n ≥ 3.
